title: Cap. IX Arg. 7 Sol: God elects some to be faithful and makes them so — he did not reprobate men that they might be unbelievers; Lombard Sent. 1 dist. 40–41
pass_a_gloss: For although God elects certain ones that they should be faithful, and by the grace of election makes them faithful, yet he is not to be said to have reprobated men that they should be unbelievers, or by reprobating to have rendered the same unbelievers. For it is the common sentence of Theologians, which the Master of the Sentences put lib. 1. dist. 40. lit. D. in these words, For not as he prepared the saints unto receiving righteousness, so did he prepare the iniquitous unto losing righteousness; because he was never a preparer of wickedness. And still more plainly, dist. 41. lit. E, It is asked whether as it is said that he elected certain ones that they should become good and faithful, so also it ought to be granted that he reprobated certain ones that they should be evil and unbelieving, and hardens that they may sin; which by no means ought to be granted. For reprobation is not so the cause of evil as predestination is the cause of good; nor does hardening so make a man evil as mercy makes him good.
pass_b_english: Though God elects some that they may be faithful, and by electing grace makes them faithful, he is not to be said to have reprobated men that they might be unbelievers, or by reprobating to have made them so. That is the common sentence of theologians, which the Master of the Sentences sets (lib. 1 dist. 40 lit. D): For not as he prepared the saints to receive righteousness did he prepare the wicked to lose it — he was never a preparer of wickedness. And still plainer (dist. 41 lit. E): it is asked whether, as he is said to have elected some that they might become good and faithful, we ought also grant he reprobated some that they might be evil and unbelieving, and hardens that they may sin — which must in no wise be granted. Reprobation is not cause of evil as predestination is cause of good; nor does hardening make a man evil as mercy makes him good.
source_text: Nam quamvis Deus eligat quosdam ut fideles essent, et per gratiam electionis eos fideles efficiat, tamen non dicendus est reprobasse homines ut infideles essent, aut reprobando eosdem infideles reddidisse. Communis enim sententia est Theologorum, quam Magister Sententiarum posuit lib. 1. dist. 40. lit. D. hisce verbis, Non enim sicut praeparavit sanctos ad justitiam percipiendam, sic praeparavit iniquos ad justitiam amittendam; quia pravitatis praeparator nunquam fuit. Et adhuc planius, dist. 41. lit. E, Quaeritur utrum sicut dicitur elegisse quosdam ut boni fierent et fideles, ita etiam concedi debeat reprobasse quosdam ut mali essent et infideles, et obdurare ut peccent; quod nullatenus concedi oportet. Non enim reprobatio ita est causa mali sicut praedestinatio est causa boni; neque obduratio ita facit hominem malum quemadmodum misericordia facit bonum.
